clue.text: Spirit label beginning to yellow

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: a brand is a trade name or label
opening letter of yellow

explanation.surface: A drinks label whose colour is turning to yellow.
explanation.definitionFit: Brandy is a distilled liquor, and spirit is the general term for strong distilled drink.

clue.text: Nosey Parker tied up by chap close to quarry

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter, so only the last one is kept

blocks.note: someone tied up is occupied, busy
bod is informal British for a person or chap
final letter of quarry

explanation.surface: An inquisitive person tied up by some man near a quarry, like a scene from a thriller.
explanation.walkthrough: A Nosey Parker is the British idiom for someone who pries into others' affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Both terms describe a meddler who pokes into other people's private business.

clue.text: In spite of everything, comes in last?

blocks.note: first meaning: nevertheless, regardless
second meaning, playful: whoever finishes last arrives behind every other runner

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second, whimsical reading: a back-marker literally finishes behind everybody.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom meaning nevertheless, and read literally it describes finishing behind every other competitor.

clue.text: Grave song?

blocks.note: surface reading: a solemn, serious piece of music
setter's reading: grave as the burial place, so a lament sung at a funeral

explanation.walkthrough: Grave reads as an adjective meaning serious, but it is also the noun for a burial plot, where a funeral lament is sung.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirge is a mournful lament performed for the dead, typically at a funeral.

clue.text: Go mad at failure to find sandal

blocks.note: to flip is to lose one's temper or go crazy
a flop is a failure

explanation.surface: Someone loses it over being unable to locate their sandal.
explanation.definitionFit: A flip-flop is a light rubber sandal held on by a thong between the toes.

clue.text: Distinctive uniform, firmly established in place where horses may be kept

definitions.text: place where horses may be kept

blocks.note: livery is the special uniform worn by servants or company staff
stable means secure, firmly fixed

explanation.surface: Smart staff uniforms have become an established fixture somewhere horses are housed.
explanation.definitionFit: A livery stable boards horses for their owners or hires them out, so it is a place horses are kept.

clue.text: Correspondent's enclosure, right, received by addict

indicators.note: something received by another is taken into it, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: a pen is an animal enclosure
a fiend is an enthusiast or addict, as in dope fiend
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A letter-writer's enclosure gets into the hands of an addict.
explanation.walkthrough: Fiend in the sense of a fanatic or addict is informal, as in a fresh-air fiend; enclosure suggests something tucked into a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen friend is someone you exchange letters with, so is a correspondent.

clue.text: Get better view on horseback

blocks.note: a look is a view
a rider is said to be up, as in a jockey mounted on a horse

explanation.surface: Climbing onto a horse gives a better view.
explanation.walkthrough: Racing reports say who is up, meaning which jockey is riding the horse.
explanation.definitionFit: When things look up they improve, so the phrasal verb means get better.

clue.text: A graven image in Pennsylvania shrine

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so the first words go within the abbreviation

blocks.note: PA is the postal abbreviation for Pennsylvania
taken as written
a graven image is a carved idol, a false god

explanation.surface: A carved idol housed in a shrine in Pennsylvania.
explanation.definitionFit: A pagoda is a tiered Buddhist or Hindu temple, a kind of sacred shrine.

clue.text: Planet — see it go round

blocks.note: it, as in having it, is sex appeal, SA
to turn is to go round

explanation.surface: An invitation to watch a planet rotate.
explanation.walkthrough: It meaning sex appeal (SA) is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturn is the sixth planet from the sun, the ringed gas giant.

clue.text: Level with boy with good service

blocks.note: level means even
a son is a boy
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Drawing level with a lad who serves well, as in a tennis match.
explanation.definitionFit: Evensong is the Anglican evening prayer service, so it is a church service.

clue.text: US writer with another novel about diamonds

indicators.note: about means going around, so the letters surround the abbreviation
novel as an adjective means new, so the letters are made into something new

blocks.note: taken as written, as the letters to rearrange
D is the card-game abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: An American author has written another book about diamonds.
explanation.walkthrough: Novel looks like a noun, the book itself, but it is the signal to rearrange the words before it, with D tucked in.
explanation.definitionFit: Edith Wharton was an American novelist, author of The Age of Innocence.

clue.text: Pub worker has to use skill during drinking bout, …

indicators.note: something happening during another is within it, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: a bender is a drinking spree
art is skill

explanation.surface: A barman needs real expertise while the customers are on a binge.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs on to 13, which continues the pub scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A bartender serves drinks behind the bar, so is someone working in a pub.

clue.text: … entire session

blocks.note: first meaning: complete
second meaning: a bout or stage

explanation.walkthrough: Read with 12, the barman stands a round of drinks, but here the word is clued twice on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Round can mean complete or whole as an adjective, and as a noun a single session or bout of activity.

clue.text: Small and attractive head backing out of shop

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so the word for head is read from end to start

blocks.note: delicate means dainty, small and pretty
a ness is a headland

explanation.surface: A dainty, pretty head backs out of a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: Head here is a geographic headland (a ness, as in Loch Ness or Dungeness), not the body part.
explanation.definitionFit: A delicatessen is a shop selling prepared foods such as cold meats and cheeses.

clue.text: Editorial about short fat eastern pantomime character

indicators.note: short means cut off, so the final letter is dropped
about means surrounding, so the editorial word wraps around the next piece

blocks.note: a column is an opinion piece in a newspaper
big means fat
E is the abbreviation for eastern

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece about a stout oriental figure from pantomime.
explanation.walkthrough: Editorial suggests a leader, but any newspaper column works. Pantomime is a British Christmas stage show descended from the harlequinade.
explanation.definitionFit: Columbine is Harlequin's sweetheart, a stock figure in traditional pantomime and harlequinade.

clue.text: Nurse drinking coffee, an untidy woman

indicators.note: someone drinking takes a liquid inside, so the beverage goes within the abbreviation

blocks.note: SRN was a State Registered Nurse in Britain
a latte is a milky coffee

explanation.surface: A nurse on her coffee break is a scruffy woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Slattern is an old-fashioned term for a slovenly, dirty or untidy woman.

clue.text: Old maid in play, endlessly strict

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter is cut off

blocks.note: to spin a record is to play it
stern means strict

explanation.surface: An elderly unmarried woman appears in a play, sternly severe.
explanation.walkthrough: Old maid is also a card game, a pull toward play, but here it is a dated term for an unmarried woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Spinster and old maid are both dated terms for an older woman who has never married.

clue.text: Now had calls, unfortunately, beginning to present an indication of disapproval

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters fall into disorder
the beginning of a word is its first letter, which alone is kept

blocks.note: taken as written, as the letters to rearrange
opening letter of present

explanation.surface: A performer, having had calls for an encore, now receives signs of displeasure.
explanation.definitionFit: A slow handclap is a slow, deliberate rhythmic clapping by an audience to show impatience or displeasure.

clue.text: A taxi picked up by American? You can count on it

indicators.note: in a down entry something picked up is lifted, so the word is read from the bottom upward

blocks.note: taken as written
a cab is a taxi
US for American, as in United States

explanation.surface: Hailing a cab in America, and a reassurance that it is dependable.
explanation.walkthrough: Picked up suggests a taxi collecting a fare; in this down clue it turns the cab upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: An abacus is a frame of beads used for counting, so you literally count on it.

clue.text: Hat left in arbour

indicators.note: a letter in something is placed inside it

blocks.note: a bower is a leafy shelter, an arbour
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A hat forgotten in a garden shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowler is a hard round felt hat, a derby in American usage.

clue.text: Sweeper needs bit of breathing space

indicators.note: a bit of a word is a small piece of it, here its first letter

blocks.note: opening letter of breathing
room is space

explanation.surface: A street cleaner needs some room to breathe.
explanation.definitionFit: A broom is a long-handled brush used for sweeping floors.

clue.text: No dead in Durham town cemetery!

indicators.note: no means without, so that letter is taken away

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for dead
Darlington is a market town in County Durham, northern England

explanation.surface: A joke that a northern English town's cemetery holds nobody dead.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the first D from the town's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Arlington National Cemetery in Virginia is the US military burial ground.

clue.text: Bovine animals by mouth of Hudson River

indicators.note: the mouth of anything is its opening, so the first letter is taken

blocks.note: neat is an old word for cattle
opening letter of Hudson

explanation.surface: Cattle grazing where the Hudson River meets the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: Hudson River suggests the American river, but the answer is a river in South Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: The Neath is a river in South Wales flowing past the town of the same name.

clue.text: Satellite phone, and its unusual ring

indicators.note: something unusual is out of the ordinary, so the letters are set in an odd arrangement

blocks.note: to phone is to call
taken as written, as letters to rearrange
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A satellite phone with a strange ringtone.
explanation.walkthrough: Satellite phone reads as one item, but the definition ends at satellite.
explanation.definitionFit: Callisto is one of the large moons of Jupiter, a natural satellite.

clue.text: Father in need of sheltered accommodation? That's very evident

blocks.note: pa is father
a tent is a shelter where campers stay

explanation.surface: Plainly an elderly dad needs a place in sheltered housing.
explanation.walkthrough: Sheltered accommodation is British housing for the elderly; read playfully it is any shelter, such as canvas.
explanation.definitionFit: Patent as an adjective means obvious or plain to see.

clue.text: Police officer, Frenchman, visiting social worker

blocks.note: Serge is a typical French man's name
an ant is a social insect and a worker

explanation.surface: A police officer and a Frenchman go to see a social worker.
explanation.walkthrough: Social worker suggests a welfare professional, but ants live in colonies and the workers do the labour.
explanation.definitionFit: A sergeant is a police rank above constable.

clue.text: Mouse star?

blocks.note: first meaning: a mouse is slang for a black eye
second meaning: something that shines brightly

explanation.walkthrough: Mouse suggests the rodent, perhaps a cartoon star like Mickey, but it is slang for a bruised eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Shiner is slang for a black eye, and literally anything that shines, such as a star.
